Here two improvements to IDG-CAL are proposed to 1) reduce the computational cost of A-terms described by more parameters and 2) optimize the set of basis functions describing the A-terms based on a stochastic model of the gain variations and the model image.

AI.tldr: The paper presents IDG-CAL, an iterative calibration algorithm using Image Domain Gridding to estimate A-terms for correcting direction dependent effects in radio astronomical imaging, proposing two enhancements to improve computational efficiency and optimize basis function selection.
AI.motivation: To address direction dependent effects in radio astronomical imaging by accurately estimating A-terms through a more efficient calibration algorithm.
AI.method: IDG-CAL utilizes the Image Domain Gridding algorithm iteratively to estimate A-terms from observed data, incorporating enhancements to reduce computational cost and optimize basis functions.
AI.result: Initial tests indicate promising results for low order A-terms, but higher order A-terms are required for deeper imaging, justifying the proposed improvements.
AI.conclusion: The proposed enhancements aim to improve both the efficiency and accuracy of A-term estimation in radio astronomy, benefiting high-quality imaging.

title: Event-by-event analysis of chiral charge separation in $p^{\uparrow}+$Au collisions within an improved AMPT model
summary: We study the charge separation induced by chiral magnetic effect (CME) in $p^{\uparrow}$+Au collisions at $\sqrt{s_{NN}}=200$ GeV event-by-event with an improved string-melting AMPT model. In this model, an impact-parameter-dependent formation-time delay is introduced to reduce the peak Bjorken energy density from $\sim$2 to $\sim$0.3 GeV/fm$^3$ and reproduces the illiptic flow $v_2(p_T)$ measured by PHENIX in $p+$Au simultaneously. The event-by-event CME source, whose quark momentum-exchange fraction scales with $|\mathbf{B}|_{\mathrm{event}}/|\mathbf{B}|_{\mathrm{max}}$ and is capped at the 7\% value from Au+Au, transmits the field geometry directly to the observable. We find that the initial correlator shows a clear scheme hierarchy tracking $B^2$. The parton cascade preserves $\sim$80--90\% of the signal, while coalescence and ART hadronic rescattering dissipate the bulk, leaving $\sim$10--30\% in the final state. The $γ_{OS}/γ_{SS}$ splitting remains visible. These results support the use of the inter-scheme difference $Δγ_{\mathrm{IV}}-Δγ_{\mathrm{II}}$ as an essentially background-free CME observable as we proposed in previous work.

AI.tldr: The study investigates charge separation due to the chiral magnetic effect (CME) in $p^{}$+Au collisions at 200 GeV, utilizing an advanced AMPT model to better align simulation outcomes with experimental data.
AI.motivation: To understand the charmed magnetic effect in particle collisions and enhance simulation accuracy in reproducing experimental observations of elliptic flow.
AI.method: The study employs an improved string-melting AMPT model incorporating an impact-parameter-dependent formation-time delay, which adjusts energy density and analyzes event-by-event CME source scaling with magnetic field geometry.
AI.result: The model successfully reproduces elliptic flow and shows that parton cascade retains 80-90% of CME signal, with significant dissipation during hadronic processes, resulting in a clear hierarchy in the initial correlator and maintaining visibility of the $γ_{OS}/γ_{SS}$ splitting.
AI.conclusion: The findings validate the use of inter-scheme differences as a background-free observable for CME, supporting previous proposals.

title: Bounds for Apparent Second-Law Violations in Quantum Trajectories
comment: 8 pages, 2 figures. Supplemental Material: 10 pages, 1 figure
summary: Negative stochastic entropy production is commonly called an apparent violation of the second law. In general quantum-trajectory dynamics, however, the physical entropy production $σ$ need not obey a forward detailed fluctuation theorem. A general arbitrary-coupling formulation identifies a dynamical-asymmetry term $σ^\ast$ that completes it into $Ω=σ+σ^\ast$, whose mean is $\langleΩ\rangle=Σ+Σ^\ast$. We prove that the likelihood-ratio sign is optimal among reversal-odd trajectory observables and use this fact to transfer an established sharp fluctuation-theorem floor to the tie-corrected physical sign statistic $Π_σ=\Pr(σ<0)+\Pr(σ=0)/2$. When $\Pr(σ=0)=0$, the result reads $\Pr(σ<0)\ge[1-\langleΩ\rangle/g(\langleΩ\rangle)]/2$, where $g$ is the inverse of $a\mapsto a\tanh(a/2)$. The physical integral fluctuation theorem simultaneously suppresses large negative events, producing a quantitative ``frequent but mild'' law, while the sign imbalance lower-bounds the hidden mean $Σ^\ast$. We formulate the measured-record protocol explicitly and illustrate and numerically audit the tie-corrected theorem in random finite-coupling collision models and a coherently driven qubit interacting with thermal ancillas.

AI.tldr: The paper explores the concept of negative stochastic entropy production in quantum trajectory dynamics, proposing a revised fluctuation theorem that incorporates a dynamical-asymmetry term, and applies it to quantify likelihood ratios and events in physical systems.
AI.motivation: To address the apparent violation of the second law of thermodynamics in quantum systems, specifically in the context of negative stochastic entropy production.
AI.method: Introduced a general arbitrary-coupling formulation that decomposes entropy production into a physical entropy component and a dynamical-asymmetry term, deriving new inequalities for negative entropy events and proposing a tie-corrected sign statistic.
AI.result: Evidenced a lower bound for the probability of negative entropy production events, which demonstrates that suppression of large negative occurrences leads to a frequent but mild law in stochastic thermodynamics, applicable to various quantum systems.
AI.conclusion: The study formulates a robust framework for understanding entropy production dynamics in quantum systems, confirming that negative entropy productions can be quantitatively evaluated and categorized, thus adding clarity to the second law of thermodynamics in these contexts.

title: Wavefront Profiling via correlation of GLAO open loop telemetry
summary: Adaptive Optics (AO) used in ground based observatories can be strengthened in both design and algorithms by a more detailed understanding of the atmosphere they seek to correct. Nowhere is this more true than on Maunakea, where a clearer profile of the atmosphere informs AO system development from the small separations of Extreme AO (ExAO) to the wide field Ground Layer AO (GLAO). Employing telemetry obtained from the 'imaka GLAO demonstrator on the University of Hawaii 2.2-meter telescope, we apply a wind profiling method that identifies turbulent layer velocities through spatial-temporal cross correlations of multiple wavefront sensors (WFSs). We compare the derived layer velocities with nearby wind anemometer data and meteorological model predictions of the upper wind speeds and discuss similarities and differences. The strengths and limitations of this profiling method are evaluated through successful recovery of injected, simulated layers into real telemetry. We detail the profilers' results, including the percentage of data with viable estimates, on four characteristic 'imaka observing runs on open loop telemetry throughout both winter and summer targets. We report on how similar layers are to external measures, the confidence of these results, and the potential for future use of this technique on other multi conjugate AO systems.

AI.tldr: The paper enhances Adaptive Optics (AO) by leveraging atmospheric insights derived from wind profiling techniques applied to data from the 'imaka GLAO demonstrator, comparing results with external wind data.
AI.motivation: To improve the design and algorithms of Adaptive Optics systems used in ground-based observatories, particularly on Maunakea, through a better understanding of the atmospheric conditions to be corrected.
AI.method: Utilizing telemetry from the 'imaka GLAO system, we apply a method that identifies turbulent layer velocities via spatial-temporal cross correlations of multiple wavefront sensors, comparing these to wind anemometer and meteorological model data.
AI.result: The wind profiling method successfully identifies turbulent layer velocities, with a high percentage of data yielding viable estimates during various observing runs, and shows good agreement with external wind measurements.
AI.conclusion: The approach demonstrates potential for future application in multi-conjugate Adaptive Optics systems, emphasizing both strengths and limitations of the profiling method.

title: Nucleon electromagnetic form factors in nonlocal chiral effective theory
summary: In this paper, we calculate the pion one-loop corrections to the electromagnetic form factors of the nucleon up to $\mathcal{O}(p^4)$ order in the nonlocal framework. To systematically investigate the role of vector-meson dominance in the model, we also include the leading-order nucleon-vector-meson coupling. Owing to the renormalization-scheme dependence of chiral low-energy coupling constants (LECs), we refit these constants to the nucleon magnetic moments, electromagnetic radii, and the $Q^2$-dependence of the electromagnetic form factors. Compared with the previous local analysis, the model results show that, in the nonlocal framework, the $Q^2$-dependence of the electromagnetic form factors in the large-$Q^2$ region is significantly improved and are consistent with experimental data.

AI.tldr: This paper presents calculations for the pion one-loop corrections to nucleon electromagnetic form factors using a nonlocal framework, refining coupling constants to align with experimental data.
AI.motivation: The study aims to improve the understanding of nucleon electromagnetic properties by including pion contributions in a nonlocal framework.
AI.method: The authors calculate pion one-loop corrections to nucleon form factors up to order $	ext{O}(p^4)$, incorporating vector-meson dominance and refitting chiral low-energy coupling constants based on nucleon magnetic moments and electromagnetic radii.
AI.result: The results indicate that the nonlocal framework provides a significantly improved description of the $Q^2$-dependence of the electromagnetic form factors in the large-$Q^2$ region, aligning well with experimental observations.
AI.conclusion: This approach shows that employing a nonlocal framework enhances the accuracy of theoretical predictions for nucleon form factors compared to previous local analysis.

title: Williamson majorization theory of fermionic non-Gaussianity
summary: Pure-state entanglement rests on a single algebraic backbone: majorization of the Schmidt spectrum governs state conversion under local operations and classical communication, and constrains entanglement monotones. Here we establish a corresponding majorization law for fermionic non-Gaussianity, the resource that elevates free fermions to universal quantum computation. Under any fermionic Gaussian protocol with pure state outcomes, the Williamson spectrum of a pure state's Majorana covariance matrix is weakly majorized by its ensemble average. This spectral law mirrors that of entanglement theory. It turns computable non-Gaussianity quantifiers such as fermionic antiflatness and occupation entropies into strong monotones for fermionic non-Gaussianity, and delivers necessary conditions and converse bounds on state conversion under Gaussian protocols. When fermion parity is conserved, no catalyst can remove a majorization obstruction---unless it carries parity coherence---and asymptotic interconversion is irreversible already for pure states. All relevant quantities are accessible from two-point Majorana correlators, turning the theory developed here into experimentally observable properties of quantum matter, testable on present-day quantum devices.

AI.tldr: This paper establishes a majorization law for fermionic non-Gaussianity, linking it to entanglement theory, and develops computable non-Gaussianity quantifiers under Gaussian protocols.
AI.motivation: To understand fermionic non-Gaussianity in the context of state conversion and resource quantification within quantum computation.
AI.method: It employs majorization theory to analyze the Williamson spectrum of a pure state's Majorana covariance matrix against its ensemble average under fermionic Gaussian protocols.
AI.result: Identifies computable quantifiers of non-Gaussianity as strong monotones, offering bounds on state conversions and showing irreversibility in fermion parity conservation cases.
AI.conclusion: The study provides a link between theoretical constructs and practical observables in quantum systems, making the findings experimentally accessible.

title: High-temperature photovoltaics for solar-electric Oberth maneuvers: ton-class payload feasibility for interstellar-precursor missions
summary: In-situ exploration beyond the giant planets remains rare because timely Solar System escape demands very high specific orbital energy, which existing concepts typically achieve only with small payloads, super-heavy launchers, or nuclear-powered propulsion. Motivated by laboratory demonstrations of high-intensity, high-temperature (HIHT) solar cells operating near $400\,^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$, we assess a solar-electric Oberth maneuver that concentrates thrust near a $0.3\,\mathrm{AU}$ perihelion. Evolutionary steering optimisation indicates that an expendable Falcon Heavy could deliver ton-class payloads to $200\,\mathrm{AU}$ within 25 years if HIHT power systems reach specific powers about $10\%$ above present-day conventional levels with a Jupiter gravity assist, or about twice those levels on a direct trajectory, under the stated assumptions. The gain stems from a threefold increase in specific orbital energy for the same $Δv$ compared with a $1\,\mathrm{AU}$ spiral. These results suggest HIHT photovoltaics could shift from survival hardware to propulsion-enabling technology for high-energy deep-space missions.

AI.tldr: This paper explores the potential of high-intensity, high-temperature solar cells for deep-space missions, proposing a solar-electric maneuver that could enable significant payload delivery to distant targets using existing launch vehicles.
AI.motivation: The study addresses the challenge of delivering large payloads beyond giant planets, where high specific orbital energy is required for timely Solar System escape.
AI.method: An analysis of a solar-electric Oberth maneuver is conducted, optimized for thrust concentration during perihelion, and feasibility is assessed using Falcon Heavy and performance benchmarks of high-temperature solar cells.
AI.result: It is projected that an expendable Falcon Heavy could deliver ton-class payloads to 200 AU within 25 years, contingent upon the enhancement of specific power levels of HIHT solar cells.
AI.conclusion: HIHT photovoltaics could transition from mere survival tools to critical enablers for propulsion in high-energy deep-space missions.

title: Probing vorticity and fluctuations in a rotating hadron resonance gas at LHC energy
summary: A large vorticity produced in non-central ultra-relativistic heavy-ion collisions induces an effective chemical potential in both partonic and hadronic matter, thereby influencing the quark-hadron transition and its associated properties. In this work, we investigate the influence of rotation on hadron yields within the framework of Hadron Resonance Gas (HRG) model. Our results show that vorticity significantly modifies hadron yields and their ratios. Most notably, rotation enhances the $p/π^+$ ratio while suppressing the $K^+/π^+$ ratio, suggesting that these observables may serve as sensitive probes of the rotational properties of the medium created in heavy-ion collisions. To quantify the effect of rotation, the calculated dependence of the $p/π^+$ ratio on vorticity is compared with the centrality dependence of the $p/π$ ratio measured by the ALICE collaboration in Pb+Pb collisions at $\sqrt{s_{_{NN}}}$ = 5.02 TeV. From this comparison, we estimate the maximum vorticity produced at freeze-out for different collision centralities. In case of peripheral collisions, the freeze-out vorticity ($ω$) is found to reach an upper bound value of approximately 0.088 GeV, whereas for central collisions it is about 0.028 GeV. Furthermore, we investigate the effect of rotation on fluctuations of conserved quantities and their correlations. This study provides a quantitative framework for assessing the role of rotation in the thermodynamics of hadronic matter and its phenomenological consequences for heavy-ion collisions.

AI.tldr: The study examines how large vorticity in non-central heavy-ion collisions affects hadron yields, revealing modifications in ratios like $p/π^+$ and $K^+/π^+$, indicating potential probes for rotational properties of the medium.
AI.motivation: To understand the effects of rotation induced by vorticity in heavy-ion collisions on quark-hadron transitions and hadron yields.
AI.method: Utilized the Hadron Resonance Gas (HRG) model to investigate the influence of rotation on hadron yields and their ratios, comparing results with experimental data from ALICE collaboration.
AI.result: Found significant modifications in hadron yield ratios due to rotation, specifically enhancing the $p/π^+$ ratio and suppressing the $K^+/π^+$ ratio; estimated maximum freeze-out vorticities for different collision centralities.
AI.conclusion: Provided a quantitative framework for analyzing the role of rotation in hadronic thermodynamics and its implications for heavy-ion collision phenomena.

title: Unextendible stabiliser bases
summary: We study incomplete sets of orthogonal stabiliser states that cannot be extended by a further stabiliser state orthogonal to all of its members. Such sets are the stabiliser analogue of unextendible product bases (UPBs), and we thus call them unextendible stabiliser bases (USBs). Leveraging the symplectic geometry underlying the $n$-qudit Pauli group in prime local dimension, we explicitly construct USBs for systems of four qubits and three qudits of odd prime local dimension. Moreover, we show that these are the respective minimal qubit, respectively qudit numbers for which such bases exist, and that USBs exist for all $n\geq4$ qubit and for all $n\geq3$ odd-prime-dimensional qudit systems. Finally, we compare the resource-theoretic aspects of USBs with those of UPBs. We establish that, analogous to the case of UPBs, the orthogonal complement of every unextendible stabiliser set is a stabiliser-free subspace, and its normalised projector is necessarily magic; moreover, it is bound magic in odd prime dimension, yet need not be for qubits. We also show that USB unextendibility alone imposes no uniform quantitative obstruction to discrimination by stabiliser operations.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces unextendible stabiliser bases (USBs), paralleling unextendible product bases, focusing on their construction, properties, and relation to resource theory.
AI.motivation: To explore incomplete orthogonal sets of stabiliser states that cannot be extended, akin to unextendible product bases, and to investigate their properties and existence for multiple qubit and qudit systems.
AI.method: Utilizing the symplectic geometry of the n-qudit Pauli group, USBs are constructed for four qubits and three qudits in odd prime dimensions, establishing essential properties of these bases.
AI.result: The authors show the minimal numbers of qubits and qudits for USB existence and demonstrate that these bases exist for all n ≥ 4 qubit systems and n ≥ 3 odd-prime-dimensional qudit systems.
AI.conclusion: USBs, like UPBs, lead to stabiliser-free subspaces, with implications for resource theory, and discrimination by stabiliser operations remains feasible despite USB unextendibility.

title: Eclipses by Artificial Satellites to Measure the Angular Sizes of Stars
comment: 25 pages; 8 figures; First released on 12 Aug 2026 to celebrate the total solar eclipse
summary:
Direct measurements of the angular sizes of stars (other than our Sun) are inherently limited by telescopes' optical diffraction limit. The spatial diffraction limit can be overcome by using time-domain information when stars are `eclipsed' by anything moving in the foreground: artificial satellites or the Moon (known as `lunar occultation imaging'). Here we analyse the angular resolution achievable by high-speed photon counting devices, when stars are eclipsed for several microseconds by one of the thousands of satellites now in low or mid-Earth orbit. We also build a full Bayesian statistical treatment for analysing simulated observations.
  We show that eclipses by the moon and satellites deliver $<2$ milliarcsecond resolution for $\sim$$10^4$ stars every year, with the diameters of $\sim$$10^1 - 10^2$ stars constrained to better than $0.5$ milliarcseconds. The application of satellites requires an ultra-fast, photon-resolving detector, capable of continuous readout with inter-frame delay controlled within $\lesssim 1$ $μ$s. Such a fast rate can easily be handled by the SPINA instrument, which has demonstrated $8$ ns inter-frame delay, and potentially by the Cherenkov Telescope Array.

AI.tldr: The study explores improving the angular resolution of star measurements during lunar occultation and satellite eclipses using high-speed photon counting, achieving resolutions <2 milliarcseconds for numerous stars.
AI.motivation: To overcome the limitations imposed by telescopes' optical diffraction when measuring the angular sizes of stars.
AI.method: Utilizing time-domain information from lunar occultation and satellite eclipses, combined with a Bayesian statistical approach for simulated data analysis.
AI.result: Eclipses provide angular resolutions of <2 milliarcseconds for ~10,000 stars annually, with diameter measurements of 10-100 stars constrained to better than 0.5 milliarcseconds.
AI.conclusion: Ultra-fast photon-resolving detectors, like the SPINA instrument, can effectively realize these resolutions, potentially extending capabilities for future observations.

title: Bayesian approach to simultaneous quantum multiparameter estimation with finite data
summary: Multiparameter estimation remains a fundamental challenge in quantum estimation theory because the optimal measurements associated with different parameters are generally incompatible. In this work, we develop a Bayesian framework for the simultaneous estimation of multiple parameters. Our approach builds on Personick's method, in which the estimation problem is reduced to a set of Lyapunov equations whose solutions define optimal observables for the individual parameters. Since these observables generally do not commute, we construct a convex combination of the solutions, parameterized by a set of variational parameters. The spectral decomposition of the resulting operator defines a parametrized projection-valued measure. The resulting projective measurement determines the likelihood function, from which the minimum mean-square error estimators and the corresponding Bayesian mean-square errors are obtained, following standard Bayesian procedures, as functions of the variational parameters. To determine their optimal values, we formulate a minimax optimization problem based on the normalized Bayesian mean-square errors, introducing a min-max normalization procedure that enables a meaningful comparison of estimation errors associated with different parameters. This optimization yields a variationally optimized projective measurement for simultaneous Bayesian estimation. Two qubit examples, involving phase estimation and the estimation of parameters defining convex combinations of unitary operations, demonstrate the construction of optimized projective measurements and the corresponding minimum mean-square error estimators within the proposed framework for finite data sets.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a Bayesian framework for multiparameter estimation in quantum systems using optimized projective measurements derived from Lyapunov equations.
AI.motivation: The challenge of simultaneous estimation of incompatible parameters in quantum estimation theory necessitates new frameworks for improving accuracy.
AI.method: The authors utilize a Bayesian approach, reducing the estimation problem to Lyapunov equations, allowing the construction of optimal observables through a variational method that yields a projective measurement.
AI.result: The results lead to the creation of a normalized min-max optimization process that identifies optimal variational parameters for Bayesian mean-square error estimators, validated through two qubit examples.
AI.conclusion: This framework provides a robust method for optimizing projective measurements in quantum parameter estimation, enhancing the accuracy of estimators for multiple parameters.

title: Scaling of soft QGP signatures in relativistic lead, xenon and oxygen collisions in EPOS4
summary: The collective expansion and hydrodynamic evolution in heavy-ion collisions is well-established. However, whether femtometer-scale droplets of QGP are produced in small systems at high energies remains a fundamental open question. Analysis of Pb$-$Pb collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}}$ = 5.02 TeV, Xe$-$Xe at $\sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}}$ = 5.44 TeV and O$-$O collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}}$ = 5.36 TeV using EPOS4 is reported to make predictions and postdictions. The results are compared with ALICE data for Pb$-$Pb and Xe$-$Xe collisions. Charged particle multiplicity (d$N_{\mathrm{ch}}$/d$η$), transverse-momentum ($p_{\mathrm{T}}$) spectra for pions ($π^{\pm}$), kaons ($K^{\pm}$), and protons ($\text{p}(\overline{\text{p}})$) are studied. The inclusion of hadronic afterburner, UrQMD (Ultra-relativistic Quantum Molecular Dynamics) is found to be necessary to correctly describe baryon yields. $p_{\mathrm{T}}$-fluctuations are also studied via normalized $p_{\mathrm{T}}$ correlator, $\sqrt{\langle \langle Δp_{\mathrm{T},i}Δp_{\mathrm{T},j} \rangle \rangle}\mathrm{/} \langle \langle p_{\mathrm{T}} \rangle \rangle$. Lastly, anisotropic flow harmonics ($v_{\mathrm{2}} \{2\}$, $v_{\mathrm{3}} \{2\}$) are computed as a function of $p_{\mathrm{T}}$ and centrality. Since EPOS4 has not been extensively studied for flow observables, this study thereby provides a non-trivial assessment of its collective dynamics. The results are compared with experiment wherever data is available. Taken together, this study provides a unified description of soft observables from Pb$-$Pb through Xe$-$Xe down to O$-$O and offer quantitative guidance on how such collisions may inform of the properties of the QGP.

AI.tldr: This study analyzes heavy-ion collisions to explore QGP production in small systems at high energies, using EPOS4 to compare results with ALICE data for various collision types.
AI.motivation: To investigate if femtometer-scale droplets of Quark-Gluon Plasma (QGP) are produced in small systems, which is an unresolved issue in heavy-ion physics.
AI.method: Analysis of Pb$-$Pb, Xe$-$Xe, and O$-$O collisions at specified energies using EPOS4 and comparing results with experimental ALICE data. Key observables include charged particle multiplicity, transverse-momentum spectra, $p_{	ext{T}}$ fluctuations, and anisotropic flow harmonics.
AI.result: The inclusion of the UrQMD afterburner is crucial for accurately describing baryon yields. Observables are systematically compared with available ALICE data for validation.
AI.conclusion: The study unifies descriptions of soft observables across different collision systems and provides insights into the properties of QGP, assessing the capability of EPOS4 in modeling collective dynamics.

title: Programmable Heisenberg-limit sensor from a nonlinear quantum energy pump
summary: We introduce a programmable Heisenberg-limited bosonic quantum sensor based on a nonlinear quantum energy pump, implemented with a Kerr-nonlinear resonator coupled to multiple high-Q microwave terminal resonators. For parameter estimation encoded in an arbitrary number-conserving Hamiltonian acting on the terminal modes, we analytically construct optimal sensing protocols that attain the maximal quantum Fisher information, including initial-state loading, probe preparation, and readout. For diagonal multiparameter signals, we further show that the full phase-sensing quantum Fisher information matrix can be obtained from correlations of locally measured physical terminal works, providing a signal-free calibration of the metrological resource. We numerically demonstrate the construction and its robustness using realistic circuit-QED parameters while including experimentally relevant imperfections.

AI.tldr: A programmable bosonic quantum sensor achieving Heisenberg limit for parameter estimation is developed, utilizing a Kerr-nonlinear resonator and high-Q microwave resonators, along with optimal sensing protocols and robustness testing.
AI.motivation: The advancement of quantum sensing technologies that maximize precision in parameter estimation is critical, particularly in the context of quantum mechanics where traditional limits can be outperformed.
AI.method: The sensor is based on a nonlinear quantum energy pump and involves constructing optimal sensing protocols for an arbitrary number-conserving Hamiltonian. It includes initial-state loading, probe preparation, and readout, along with deriving the quantum Fisher information matrix from local measurements of terminal works.
AI.result: The full phase-sensing quantum Fisher information matrix can be obtained through correlations of terminal works, yielding a signal-free calibration method. Numerical demonstrations validate the effectiveness and robustness of this sensor under realistic conditions and imperfections.
AI.conclusion: The proposed sensor represents an innovative approach to achieving Heisenberg-limited precision in quantum metrology, offering potential applications in various quantum information tasks.

title: Baryogenesis and CMB spectral distortion from Axions
summary: We discuss a mechanism for generating the baryon asymmetry in the early universe. We show that an axion-like particle can modify the related gauge field configurations in the Standard Model, thereby altering their dispersion relations. This change in the Chern-Simons number can source a violation of baryon number. We derive the relationship between the resulting baryon number and the evolution of the axion background. We estimate the baryon asymmetry produced via this mechanism and show that the observed value can be naturally achieved. We also show that axion photon coupling produces Cosmic Microwave Background spectral distortion. Our results show that the resulting distortion approaches a constant at low frequencies, unlike the conventional y-type and $μ$-type distortions.

AI.tldr: The paper presents a mechanism for generating baryon asymmetry in the early universe using an axion-like particle, which modifies gauge field configurations in the Standard Model to produce baryon number violation, potentially achieving observed baryon asymmetry levels while also affecting Cosmic Microwave Background spectral characteristics.
AI.motivation: To explore a novel mechanism for baryon asymmetry generation in the early universe and to relate it to axion-like particles.
AI.method: The authors analyze how an axion-like particle alters gauge field configurations of the Standard Model, influencing dispersion relations and leading to baryon number violation through changes in the Chern-Simons number.
AI.result: The study derives the relationship between baryon number production and the evolution of the axion background, estimating that the resultant baryon asymmetry can align with observational values. Furthermore, it identifies unique features in Cosmic Microwave Background distortion linked to axion photon coupling.
AI.conclusion: The proposed mechanism offers a natural way to achieve the observed baryon asymmetry and provides a distinctive low-frequency behavior in Cosmic Microwave Background distortion compared to conventional models.

title: Wave-particle-mixedness redistribution in Schwarzschild spacetime
summary: The redistribution of the wave feature, particle feature, and mixedness is investigated for two-qubit isotropic states in Schwarzschild spacetime under Hawking radiation and environmental decoherence. It is shown that Hawking radiation changes their relative weights among different horizon regions rather than simply suppressing them. The analysis is further extended to phase damping, phase flip, and bit flip channels. Phase damping monotonically suppresses the wave feature and enhances mixedness, phase flip produces a symmetric death-and-revival behavior of the wave feature, and bit flip mainly reshapes the particle feature and mixedness through diagonal population redistribution. However, although Hawking radiation and channel noise affect the distribution of wave feature, particle feature, and mixedness in the subsystems, the triality relation among them still holds and remains unaffected by thermal and environmental noises.

AI.tldr: This study explores the effects of Hawking radiation and environmental decoherence on wave features, particle features, and mixedness in two-qubit isotropic states in Schwarzschild spacetime.
AI.motivation: To understand how Hawking radiation and different channels affect the foundational properties of quantum states in curved spacetime.
AI.method: The study examines the redistribution of quantum features under Hawking radiation and various noise channels (phase damping, phase flip, bit flip).
AI.result: Hawking radiation alters the relative weights of quantum features across horizon regions; different channels have distinct effects on these features, but the triality relation remains intact.
AI.conclusion: Triality among wave feature, particle feature, and mixedness is preserved despite the impact of thermal and environmental noise.

title: Symmetrized Block-Product Periodic Marginals in Infinite Translation-Invariant Quantum Chains
summary: We study local marginals in one-dimensional translation-invariant quantum systems that may hide finite-period structure. Given an $n$-site reduced density matrix, we ask whether it can be obtained by repeating a finite $p$-site block state along the chain and averaging over the $p$ lattice translations. This defines a symmetrized block-product periodic marginal problem, which provides a route both to diagnosing hidden periodic order from local data and to upper bounding ground-state energy densities of infinite translation-invariant local Hamiltonians. We develop two complementary methods. The first is a semidefinite-programming relaxation based on block permutation symmetry and positive partial transpose constraints, which outer-approximates the convex hull of such marginals and yields certified infeasibility tests. The second is a symmetrized matrix product state ansatz, which constructs explicit block-product periodic states and gives variational upper bounds. We benchmark the framework on the Majumdar-Ghosh model, transverse-field Ising, XX, XXZ, and contextuality-related spin models. The results show that the method captures the expected finite-period structure in exactly solvable cases and gives systematically improving variational energies as the period and bond dimension increase. We also formulate a periodic-NPA relaxation for translation-invariant contextuality witnesses and recover the known quantum limits in the tested examples.

AI.tldr: The paper investigates local marginals in one-dimensional translation-invariant quantum systems to identify hidden periodic structures using a symmetrized block-product approach, while also proposing methods for bounding ground-state energy densities.
AI.motivation: To diagnose hidden periodic order from local data in quantum systems and upper bound ground-state energy densities of infinite translation-invariant Hamiltonians.
AI.method: Two methods: 1. Semidefinite-programming relaxation based on block permutation symmetry and positive partial transpose constraints; 2. A symmetrized matrix product state ansatz for constructing explicit block-product periodic states.
AI.result: The framework successfully identifies finite-period structures in solvable models and provides improved variational energy estimates as period and bond dimension increase.
AI.conclusion: Periodic-NPA relaxation for contextuality witnesses recovers known quantum limits, confirming the methods' effectiveness in handling periodic structure in quantum systems.

title: Private Correlations Certify Sensing Capability
summary: We show that private correlations in a bipartite quantum state constitute a metrological resource for distributed sensing assisted by a possibly noisy channel from one party to the other. We begin with an example with distillable secret key but poor locally accessible sensing performance and show that an assisting channel substantially improves its performance. We then prove a general theorem showing that positive private information in the encoding basis certifies a quantitative lower bound on the locally accessible sensing capability after assistance. We further show that classical correlations alone provide no analogous guarantee, whereas, in the absence of the assisting subsystem, the privacy-based guarantee reduces to an entanglement-based one. Finally, in a channel formulation, we show that a channel with positive private information allows nonzero locally accessible sensitivity when paired with a suitable assisting channel.

AI.tldr: Quantum states with private correlations enhance distributed sensing performance, especially when assisted by noisy channels.
AI.motivation: To explore how private correlations in bipartite quantum states can serve as a resource for improving distributed sensing capabilities, especially in noisy environments.
AI.method: The paper presents an example of a bipartite quantum state with distillable secret key, develops a theorem linking private information to sensing performance, and contrasts outcomes with classical correlations.
AI.result: A positive correlation of private information guarantees a lower bound on locally accessible sensing performance post-assistance, unlike classical correlations, which offer no such guarantee.
AI.conclusion: The presence of positive private information in channels can mitigate noise effects and improve sensitivity in distributed sensing, confirming the utility of quantum resources over classical ones.

title: Monsters and neutron stars
summary: Using dimensional arguments and other simple estimates, it is pointed out that a branch of nuclei with mass number A>10^7 could be metastable if they have close to maximal isospin. This branch is continuous with neutron stars. The fastest decay mode of these hypothetical metastable nuclei (which we call monsters) is through neutron evaporation. We present an estimate of the lifetime and show it could be more than 100 ps for A>10^{39}. We speculate about their creation in binary neutron star mergers, where we argue that their lifetimes could be extended further, and their presence could be detectable in gravity wave experiments of the near future.

AI.tldr: The paper discusses the potential metastability of nuclei with mass numbers greater than 10^7, suggesting they could exist in neutron stars and estimating their decay times and potential detection in future experiments.
AI.motivation: To explore the possibility of metastable nuclei with high mass numbers and their implications in astrophysics, particularly in relation to neutron stars and gravitational wave detection.
AI.method: Utilization of dimensional arguments and estimates to analyze the properties and decay modes of hypothetical metastable nuclei.
AI.result: Estimates suggest that these 'monsters' could have lifetimes exceeding 100 ps for mass numbers greater than 10^{39} and may be created in binary neutron star mergers.
AI.conclusion: The metastable nuclei have implications for astrophysical phenomena and potential detection in future gravitational wave experiments.

title: A Single Atom in Front of a Mirror is a Universal Reservoir Computer
summary: Universal approximation in reservoir computing is typically associated with a class of reservoirs. We show that universality can be associated with a single reservoir, considering a minimal setup of a single atom in front of a mirror. In its linear-transducer limit, our reservoir is a universal approximator of fading-memory maps under an operating class of checkable conditions, with a rate constant measured at the operating point. A given reservoir can reach arbitrary accuracy by changing measurement settings. The proof gives an explicit recipe: for a target accuracy, it specifies the required physical resources and resonator modes. Enlarging the number of accessible modes increases the matchable kernel span without reducing capability. Beyond the linear limit, the atom's saturation replaces high-order polynomial readouts, and the device operates on real-world tasks alongside classical baselines. Our results highlight an example of universality with a minimal quantum setup.

AI.tldr: The paper demonstrates that a single atom near a mirror can serve as a universal approximator in reservoir computing, providing a strategy to achieve high accuracy by adjusting measurement settings.
AI.motivation: To explore the concept of universality in reservoir computing using a minimal quantum system rather than a class of reservoirs.
AI.method: A simplified setup of a single atom in front of a mirror is analyzed, focusing on its linear-transducer limit to establish it as a universal approximator of fading-memory maps.
AI.result: The proposed reservoir can achieve arbitrary accuracy with specific measurement settings and physical resources. Increasing the number of resonator modes enhances the kernel span without compromising capabilities.
AI.conclusion: The study demonstrates that a simple quantum setup can exemplify universality in reservoir computing, suitable for real-world applications.

title: Gluonic nucleon energy correlators and fracture functions for Color Glass Condensate
summary: Nucleon energy correlators (NECs) and fracture functions provide novel tools for probing nucleon and nuclear structure at small $x$ through measurements in the target fragmentation region (TFR) of deep inelastic scattering (DIS). We investigate gluonic NECs and fracture functions using the Color Glass Condensate effective theory at eikonal accuracy. We find that only the unpolarized and linearly polarized gluon components in an unpolarized target are nonvanishing at this order, and that both are determined by the adjoint dipole $S$-matrix. Furthermore, we show that the linearly polarized gluonic NEC $h_{1}^{t,g}$ generates a characteristic $\cos 2φ$ azimuthal asymmetry in the DIS energy pattern in the TFR. Unlike analogous observables in the current fragmentation region, this asymmetry is governed by the ratio of the linearly polarized gluon NEC $h_{1}^{t,g}$ to the unpolarized quark NEC $f_{1}^{q}$, making it particularly sensitive to the saturation scale. Our numerical analysis shows that this asymmetry exhibits substantial nuclear suppression, providing a novel window into the onset of gluon saturation at the future Electron-Ion Collider.

AI.tldr: The paper explores gluonic nucleon energy correlators and fracture functions, highlighting their role in understanding nucleon structure during deep inelastic scattering, particularly focusing on azimuthal asymmetries and gluon saturation.
AI.motivation: To investigate nucleon and nuclear structure at small $x$ using advanced theoretical frameworks and detail the role of gluonic components in deep inelastic scattering.
AI.method: The study employs the Color Glass Condensate effective theory at eikonal accuracy to analyze gluonic NECs and fracture functions, focusing on their dependency on the adjoint dipole $S$-matrix.
AI.result: It is found that only the unpolarized and linearly polarized gluon components contribute non-zero values, leading to the observation of a $	ext{cos} 2φ$ azimuthal asymmetry in the target fragmentation region, influenced by the ratio of linearly polarized gluon NEC to unpolarized quark NEC.
AI.conclusion: The findings suggest significant nuclear suppression of the asymmetry, indicating a new approach to exploring gluon saturation phenomena at the future Electron-Ion Collider.

title: Simultaneous Heisenberg-Limited Multiparameter Metrology via Indefinite Evolution
summary: Quantum metrology achieves Heisenberg-limited precision in single-parameter estimation, but its multiparameter extension is fundamentally constrained by both parameter-encoding and measurement incompatibility. Noncommuting signal generators may cause incompatible parameter-encoding, preventing the quantum Fisher information matrix from simultaneously achieving the Heisenberg scale for all parameters. Due to incompatible optimal measurements, the classical Fisher information matrix represents the practical attainable precision. Here, we introduce a multiparameter metrology framework based on indefinite evolution (IE), in which different control operations and signal reversal are placed in a coherent superposition. For a single-qubit probe with mutually orthogonal signal generators, IE enables compatible parameter encoding and optimal measurement without the signal reversal. For parallel generators, where only signal reversal realized by its generator is available, IE can achieve the same performance. We further extend this mechanism to noisy, many-body, and high-dimensional probes, and establish general conditions for achieving the simultaneous Heisenberg-limit. In contrast, definite evolution cannot achieve the same performance under compatible optimal measurements, even when signal reversal is available. Our results identify IE as an operational resource for overcoming multiparameter incompatibility and open a route toward attainable Heisenberg-limited sensing in interferometric platforms.

AI.tldr: This study proposes an indefinite evolution framework to improve multiparameter quantum metrology, enabling Heisenberg-limited precision through compatible parameter encoding and optimal measurements.
AI.motivation: To overcome the limitations of quantum metrology in multiparameter estimation due to measurement incompatibility and parameter-encoding issues.
AI.method: Introduces an indefinite evolution (IE) framework that uses coherent superposition for control operations and signal reversal, allowing for compatible parameter encoding in single-qubit probes and extends this to multi-parameter scenarios.
AI.result: IE enables achieving Heisenberg-limit precision for both single and multiple parameters, even in noisy and high-dimensional systems, outperforming definite evolution methods.
AI.conclusion: Indefinite evolution is a valuable resource for enhancing multiparameter quantum metrology, paving the way for advanced sensing capabilities in interferometric settings.

title: State-Dependent Visibility of Non-Commutative Ordering in Quantum Dynamics
summary: A nonzero commutator proves that two orderings differ as operators, but it does not ensure that a physical state can reveal the difference. We ask when non-Abelian ordering information becomes dynamically invisible. For Hermitian operators $B$ and $C$, we compare the evolutions generated by the opposite-order products $M=(B+iC)(B-iC)$ and $\widetilde M=(B-iC)(B+iC)$, and define their operational visibility from the minimum overlap of the output states over a normalized time window. This visibility bounds the difference produced by the two orderings in every observable on the chosen state. An exact one-qubit solution shows that the same fixed pair can be perfectly invisible in one state and visible in another. We then keep the ordered generators fixed and vary only the many-body ground state across a quantum phase transition. The same ordering difference is nearly invisible in one regime and clearly visible in the other. Moreover, states with identical leading quadratic decay can develop sharply different finite-time visibility because their first distinction appears at higher order. The effect persists across distinct operator pairs and coefficient perturbations. Thus dynamical Abelianization is a property of the state-dependent process, i.e., non-Abelian ordering information can become operationally inaccessible even though the underlying operators remain non-commuting.

AI.tldr: This study explores when non-Abelian ordering information becomes dynamically invisible, using Hermitian operators to analyze state visibility across different quantum states. It finds that dynamical Abelianization can occur, rendering distinct operator orderings operationally indistinguishable in certain states.
AI.motivation: To understand the implications of non-Abelian operator orderings in quantum mechanics and their visibility in physical states, especially across quantum phase transitions.
AI.method: The authors compare the evolution of two orderings of Hermitian operators $B$ and $C$ by analyzing the output states they produce and defining operational visibility based on their overlap over time.
AI.result: An exact solution demonstrates state-dependent visibility of operator orderings, where the same pair can be invisible in one state and visible in another, revealing that different regimes of many-body ground states exhibit varying visibility of operator orderings.
AI.conclusion: Non-Abelian ordering information may become operationally inaccessible despite the operators being non-commuting, highlighting a dynamic dependence on the quantum state involved.

title: Multi-Channel Di-Higgs Production in the scNMSSM: From Exotic 8b to Boosted 8tau Signatures at the HL-LHC
summary: We investigate multi-channel di-Higgs signal prospects in the semi-constrained Next-to-Minimal Supersymmetric Standard Model (scNMSSM) at large-lambda/low-tan(beta) at the HL-LHC with sqrt(s) = 13.6 TeV and L = 3000 fb^{-1}. Building on our previous work, four benchmark points are selected from 66 viable SM-like candidates, spanning three di-Higgs topologies: exotic multi-b (h1h1 -> 4a1 -> 8b, BP1/BP3), boosted multi-tau (h1h1 -> 4a1 -> 8tau, BP2), and SM-like (BP4). A complete signal simulation chain (MadGraph5_aMC@NLO + Pythia 8.316 + Delphes 3) is employed for 10^5 signal events per benchmark point. Background yields are estimated from published LHC analyses and are used only for indicative sensitivity projections. For the 8b topology (BP1: m_{a1} = 47.4 GeV, BP3: m_{a1} = 51.9 GeV), b-jet efficiencies of epsilon(>=4b) ~ 14% yield S ~ 14,000-16,000 events, potentially compatible with 5-sigma sensitivity under the simplified background model adopted. For the boosted 8tau topology (BP2: m_{a1} = 8.2 GeV), 82.4% of same-a1 tau-pairs have Delta R(tau,tau) < 0.4, below the standard jet cone radius, due to the large Lorentz boost gamma ~ 7.5. This topology yields epsilon(>=2tau) = 38.4%, a factor of ~21 above the SM baseline, but requires dedicated boosted a1 taggers due to irreducible multi-tau backgrounds. BP4 serves as a SM-like reference, consistent with existing HL-LHC HH projections. The Higgs self-coupling modifier kappa_lambda in [0.884, 0.951] is universally suppressed below unity. The boosted a1 topology of BP2 is not covered by any existing ATLAS or CMS di-Higgs search, strongly motivating dedicated sub-jet analysis strategies at the HL-LHC.

AI.tldr: This study explores di-Higgs signals in the scNMSSM framework at the HL-LHC, identifying key benchmark points across different topologies and evaluating their potential for detection.
AI.motivation: To assess the prospects of detecting multi-channel di-Higgs signals in the semi-constrained Next-to-Minimal Supersymmetric Standard Model, especially in unexplored decay channels.
AI.method: The authors simulate di-Higgs signals using MadGraph5_aMC@NLO, Pythia 8.316, and Delphes 3 for various benchmark points, estimating background yields from published LHC analyses.
AI.result: The study finds significant event yields for the 8b topology and improved efficiencies for the 8tau topology, highlighting the need for specialized tagging techniques.
AI.conclusion: The boosted a1 topology is not currently covered by existing di-Higgs searches, warranting dedicated analysis strategies at the HL-LHC to enhance detection capabilities.

title: Unified Exact Cylindrical Dirac Modes and Symmetry-Resolved Quantum Geometry
summary: Exact cylindrical solutions of the free Dirac equation provide natural single-particle modes for a broad class of axially symmetric relativistic fermion systems, including electron vortices, twisted-particle scattering, rotating matter, and cylindrical field quantization, but are commonly formulated in different internal bases. We derive the general regular positive-energy cylindrical solution at fixed energy, transverse and longitudinal momenta, and total angular momentum, and show how the commonly used spin-polarized, separation, helicity, and transverse-helicity modes are embedded in the resulting two-dimensional solution space. A conserved transverse operator resolves the residual doublet into two symmetry-defined branches. Their parameter-dependent eigenspaces admit a gauge-invariant quantum-geometric characterization, with opposite Berry curvatures, a common quantum metric, and saturation of the two-level metric--curvature relation. We further derive symmetry constraints on branch conversion and the corresponding reduced two-state dynamics. The resulting framework connects mode classification, symmetry resolution, quantum geometry, and dynamics across distinct cylindrical Dirac settings.

AI.tldr: This paper derives a unified framework for cylindrical solutions of the free Dirac equation, revealing the connections between various modes, quantum geometry, and dynamics in axially symmetric fermion systems.
AI.motivation: To provide a coherent understanding of the cylindrical solutions in the Dirac equation and their applications in various relativistic fermion systems.
AI.method: The authors derive a general positive-energy cylindrical solution using fixed parameters, then embed commonly used modes into this framework while analyzing their eigenspaces and quantum-geometric characteristics.
AI.result: The paper showcases the existence of two symmetry-defined branches in the solution space and their gauge-invariant quantum-geometric properties, such as opposite Berry curvatures and a common quantum metric.
AI.conclusion: The proposed framework integrates mode classification, symmetry resolution, and quantum geometry, facilitating the understanding of dynamics across different cylindrical Dirac scenarios.

title: Tricritical dynamics in $\mathrm{^3He}$-$\mathrm{^4He}$ mixtures and QCD
summary: In this paper we study the universal critical dynamics near the tricritical points in $\mathrm{^3He}$-$\mathrm{^4He}$ mixtures and QCD with two massless quark flavors. In particular, we use the real-time formulation of the functional renormalization group to understand how the tricritical region connects the $O(4)$ Model G dynamics of the two-flavor chiral phase transition to that of Model H for the QCD critical point with explicitly broken chiral symmetry. We show that in presence of an additional subdiffusive energy-like density, the tricritical dynamics inherits the strong dynamic scaling of Model G, where the critical fluctuations of order parameter and conserved $O(N)$ charges relax at identical rates. The strong scaling in the planar $O(2)$ case relevant for the $λ$-line and the tricritical point in the liquid $\mathrm{^3He}$-$\mathrm{^4He}$ mixtures arises as an interesting limiting case. Including the explicit symmetry breaking by the finite light-quark masses in QCD, the energy-like density of the tricritical dynamics mixes linearly with the $Z_2$ order parameter to eventually produce the characteristic slow fluctuations of the entropy per baryon near the QCD critical point.

AI.tldr: This paper explores critical dynamics near tricritical points in 3He4He mixtures and QCD, using functional renormalization group techniques to connect models and study the effects of symmetries and energy densities.
AI.motivation: To understand the universal critical dynamics at tricritical points in 3He and 4He mixtures, as well as in QCD with massless quark flavors, focusing on how these phenomena relate to different theoretical models.
AI.method: Utilized the real-time functional renormalization group to analyze the dynamics and scaling behaviors of critical fluctuations in relation to Model G and Model H, particularly under the influence of subdiffusive density.
AI.result: Identified that tricritical dynamics adopt strong dynamic scaling characteristics of Model G, with critical fluctuations and conserved charges relaxing at identical rates, especially highlighting the case for the planar O(2) model in liquid mixtures.
AI.conclusion: The mixing of energy-like density with the $Z_2$ order parameter leads to slow entropy fluctuations near the QCD critical point, indicating intricate relationships between symmetry breaking and critical dynamics.

title: Stream Decoding with Confidence Scores at Room and Cryogenic Temperatures
summary: In fault-tolerant quantum computing, fast and accurate decoding is crucial. Snowflake is a decoder for the surface code that runs in a streaming fashion. In this paper, we implement Snowflake on commercial FPGAs and validate them at room and cryogenic temperatures. Our results demonstrate high decoding throughput for small code distances that, when extrapolated, remains within acceptable limits for larger distances. Further, we incorporate the calculation of certain decoder confidence scores with negligible overhead both in terms of latency and physical resource utilisation. We note that implementing a large-scale system would require either a large FPGA beyond today's technology or clusters of FPGAs connected via a high-speed bus. Thus, we discuss an alternative architecture that exploits the locality of Snowflake by processing 2D slices of the 3D decoding window and offloading segments of the 3D structure to a high-speed memory.

AI.tldr: This paper presents an implementation of the Snowflake decoder for fault-tolerant quantum computing on commercial FPGAs, showing high throughput and suggesting an alternative architecture for large-scale systems.
AI.motivation: Fast and accurate decoding is essential in fault-tolerant quantum computing, particularly for the surface code.
AI.method: Snowflake decoder is implemented on FPGAs, tested at room and cryogenic temperatures, and includes confidence score calculations with low overhead.
AI.result: High decoding throughput for small code distances; projections show feasibility for larger distances; confidence scores are added with minimal resource impact.
AI.conclusion: Large-scale systems may require advanced FPGA technology or clusters; an architecture using 2D processing slices and high-speed memory is proposed for scalability.

title: Generating GKP states using quantum dots inside a strongly coupled cavity
summary: GKP states enable fault-tolerant CV quantum computation, but their generation remains experimentally challenging due to their highly non-Gaussian and infinite-energy ideal structure. In this work, we present a realistic and scalable protocol for generating finite-energy resource states, specifically the qunaught state, using Schrodinger cat states generated in a strongly coupled quantum dot-cavity system. Our scheme combines deterministic squeezed cat-state generation, cat-breeding protocols, and homodyne measurements. Using numerical simulations, we analyze the role of various parameters of the quantum dot-cavity system in the generation of practical qunaught states. Furthermore, we quantify the trade-off between the fidelity and generation probability of these states and exploit the fact that accepting a structured set of homodyne outcomes can significantly enhance the overall success rate. The proposed approach is compatible with integrated photonics and telecom wavelengths, offering a promising route toward scalable CV quantum information processing.

AI.tldr: The paper presents a protocol for generating finite-energy qunaught states using squeezed cat states in a quantum dot-cavity system, addressing the challenge of high non-Gaussianity in GKP states.
AI.motivation: To overcome the experimental challenges in generating fault-tolerant CV quantum computation states due to their ideal infinite-energy structure.
AI.method: The authors propose a protocol that utilizes deterministic squeezed cat-state generation, cat-breeding protocols, and homodyne measurements, validated through numerical simulations.
AI.result: The study analyzes parameter influences on qunaught state generation and shows that selective homodyne outcomes can enhance success rates, balancing fidelity and generation probability.
AI.conclusion: The proposed generation scheme is compatible with integrated photonics, providing a feasible path for scalable continuous-variable quantum information processing.

title: QCD Vacuum in an Inhomogeneous Magnetic Field
summary: The effect of an inhomogeneous magnetic field on the QCD vacuum is addressed using the framework of chiral perturbation theory. The magnetic field is chosen to be localized along one spatial direction, with a profile for which the underlying quantum mechanical problem is exactly solvable. Particular attention is paid to regularization and renormalization using dimensional regularization. While the non-vanishing gradient of the magnetic field requires additional operators in chiral perturbation theory, their effect occurs at next-to-next-to-leading order in the chiral expansion. Consequently, the magnetic field dependence of equilibrium vacuum observables can be determined at next-to-leading order without undetermined parameters. We compute the zero-temperature free energy and chiral condensate for the inhomogeneous background, both as integrated quantities as well as spatially resolved local observables. Comparison with locally constant approximations enables a direct probe of the spatial response and nonlocal structure of the magnetized QCD vacuum. We additionally derive the induced vacuum current associated with the inhomogeneity of the magnetic field.

AI.tldr: The paper investigates the influence of an inhomogeneous magnetic field on the QCD vacuum using chiral perturbation theory, focusing on the effects at next-to-leading order without undetermined parameters.
AI.motivation: To explore how inhomogeneous magnetic fields affect the QCD vacuum, enhancing understanding of vacuum properties in quantum chromodynamics (QCD).
AI.method: Utilizing chiral perturbation theory with a localized magnetic field profile, the paper employs dimensional regularization for renormalization and computes vacuum observables at next-to-leading order.
AI.result: The zero-temperature free energy and chiral condensate are calculated, revealing spatially resolved observables that highlight the response and nonlocal structure of the magnetized QCD vacuum.
AI.conclusion: The study provides insights into the effects of inhomogeneous magnetic fields on the QCD vacuum, enabling comparisons to constant field approximations, and derives the vacuum current linked to the magnetic field inhomogeneity.

title: Nanoscale graphitization and defect evolution in silicon-vacancy center-containing nanodiamonds under high-pressure high-temperature annealing
summary: Group-IV color centers, such as the silicon-vacancy (SiV) defect, are highly promising for solid-state quantum technologies. However, nanodiamonds typically exhibit significant lattice strain and structural disorder, which degrade their optical properties and hinder the resolution of the fine spectral structure at cryogenic temperatures. High-pressure high-temperature (HPHT) annealing offers a potential route to relax internal strain, although the phase stability of diamond at the nanoscale under such conditions remains poorly constrained. Here, we investigate the structural evolution of nanodiamonds during HPHT annealing using a Paris-Edinburgh press coupled with in situ synchrotron X-ray diffraction at SOLEIL. A dedicated sample assembly combining nanodiamonds - NaCl - Pt enabled accurate pressure-temperature calibration and real-time monitoring of phase transformations. The diffraction data reveal that the onset of diamond-to-graphite transition occurs at approximately 1800 K at 2 GPa and 2120 K at 4 GPa under the applied HPHT heating protocol. These experimentally determined graphitization onsets define a practical pressure-temperature processing window for HPHT annealing of nanodiamonds while avoiding detectable graphitization and provide a calibrated framework for reliable off-beam annealing treatments that avoid graphitization. Photoluminescence measurements on samples annealed below the graphitization threshold show improved optical response, with partial resolution of the SiV fine structure at 12 K. These optical measurements suggest a relationship between nanoscale phase stability and the optical response of individual SiV-containing nanodiamonds following HPHT annealing. The experimentally established HPHT processing window provides a practical framework for the controlled processing of quantum nanodiamonds while avoiding graphitization.

AI.tldr: This study examines the effects of high-pressure high-temperature (HPHT) annealing on the structural stability and optical properties of nanodiamonds containing silicon-vacancy (SiV) defects.
AI.motivation: Enhancement of optical properties in nanodiamonds is crucial for solid-state quantum technologies, but lattice strain and structural disorder hinder their performance.
AI.method: Nanodiamonds underwent HPHT annealing within a Paris-Edinburgh press, utilizing in situ synchrotron X-ray diffraction to monitor structural changes and determine graphitization thresholds.
AI.result: Graphitization onset was identified at approximately 1800 K at 2 GPa and 2120 K at 4 GPa, establishing a safe processing window for HPHT treatment without inducing graphitization. Improved photoluminescence in nanodiamonds processed below these thresholds validated the findings.
AI.conclusion: The established HPHT processing window provides a reliable framework for enhancing the optical characteristics of SiV-containing nanodiamonds, aiding their application in quantum technologies.

title: $|ΔI|=3/2$ non-leptonic hyperon decays in covariant baryon chiral perturbation theory
summary: Inspired by the recent BESIII measurements of non-leptonic hyperon decays, we reexamine their $|ΔI|=3/2$ amplitudes in covariant baryon chiral perturbation theory with the extended-on-mass-shell renormalization scheme. Using the same restricted set of diagrammatic topologies as in the early analyses in heavy baryon chiral perturbation theory, we assess the effects of relativistic corrections, explicit decuplet baryons, different spin-$3/2$ coupling schemes, and pion-loop contributions. Our results show that relativistic effects alone lead to only mild changes, while decuplet contributions, especially in the consistent-coupling scheme, significantly improve the fit quality. Pion-loop contributions further reduce the $χ^2$ values. We highlight the importance of the consistent coupling scheme in the decuplet sector for describing the selected $|ΔI|=3/2$ amplitudes.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes non-leptonic hyperon decay amplitudes using baryon chiral perturbation theory, focusing on relativistic corrections and decuplet baryon contributions.
AI.motivation: To clarify the behavior of non-leptonic hyperon decay amplitudes in light of recent BESIII measurements.
AI.method: Reexamination of $|ΔI|=3/2$ amplitudes using baryon chiral perturbation theory, considering relativistic effects, decuplet baryons, and pion-loops.
AI.result: Relativistic effects have mild impacts, while decuplet contributions enhance fit quality considerably, especially using the consistent-coupling scheme.
AI.conclusion: The consistent coupling scheme in the decuplet sector is crucial for accurately describing the $|ΔI|=3/2$ amplitudes.

title: Zero transfer on mixed graphs
summary: In this paper, we investigate zero transfer on mixed graphs. Zero transfer is a quantum walk phenomenon in which the transition amplitude between two vertices is identically zero for all times, so that no quantum state transfer occurs between them. Using the Hermitian adjacency matrix, we derive necessary and sufficient conditions for zero transfer in mixed graphs. We then specialize these criteria to oriented circulant graphs, obtaining nonexistence results for prime order, structural restrictions for even order, and exhaustive computational classifications for small orders.

AI.tldr: This paper examines zero transfer in mixed graphs, establishing conditions for no quantum state transfer using the Hermitian adjacency matrix and applying results to oriented circulant graphs.
AI.motivation: To understand the conditions under which quantum state transfer fails in mixed graphs, as explored through the phenomenon of zero transfer.
AI.method: The authors derive necessary and sufficient conditions for zero transfer in mixed graphs using the Hermitian adjacency matrix, and specialize these results to oriented circulant graphs.
AI.result: They find nonexistence results for prime order and structural restrictions for even order, along with comprehensive classifications for small orders.
AI.conclusion: The research enhances the understanding of quantum walk phenomena in specific graph types, contributing valuable insights into the structure of mixed graphs.

title: Photonic realization of a subgraph extraction in a quantum random network
summary: Understanding how complex connectivity emerges in networks is a fundamental challenge in classical and quantum science. In classical random networks, complex subgraphs typically require relatively high connection probabilities, whereas quantum random network theory predicts that such structures can arise at a single, lower threshold through entanglement and local operations. Here, using an integrated silicon photonic chip, we experimentally realize a quantum subgraph predicted by quantum random network theory in a four-node quantum random network. Our integrated platform exploits probabilistic photon-pair sources and coherent control of path modes to prepare a structured quantum subgraph through local transformations and postselection, operating in a threshold regime that differs from classical random networks. We verify that the subgraph state exhibits genuine high-dimensional multipartite entanglement across the nodes, providing experimental evidence that quantum entanglement enables connectivity structures beyond classical accessibility.

AI.tldr: This paper explores how complex connectivity in networks can be achieved in quantum networks through entanglement at a lower threshold compared to classical networks, experimentally demonstrating this in a four-node setup.
AI.motivation: The study aims to understand the emergence of complex connectivity in networks, particularly in distinguishing between classical and quantum theories.
AI.method: An integrated silicon photonic chip is used to create a four-node quantum random network, leveraging photon-pair sources and local transformations through postselection.
AI.result: The experiment successfully realized a quantum subgraph that demonstrates genuine high-dimensional multipartite entanglement among the nodes.
AI.conclusion: The findings provide experimental proof that quantum entanglement allows for complex connectivity structures that classical networks cannot achieve.

title: Quantum Computing for Industrial Electromagnetics: Applicability and Case Studies in Solving Maxwell's Equations
summary:
Computational electromagnetics plays a central role in many industrial applications but often requires substantial computational resources, particularly when fine spatial discretizations are needed. While classical approaches remain the standard, quantum computing offers the potential to accelerate large-scale simulations by encoding them with a limited number of qubits.
  Here, we investigate the performance and resource scaling of the Harrow-Hassidim-Lloyd (HHL) and Quantum Singular Value Transformation (QSVT) algorithms for solving linear systems generated by the finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) method, a widely adopted numerical scheme for discretizing Maxwell's equations. We benchmark their performance across representative industrial use cases, including radar propagation, lens simulations, and beamforming processes. Our results demonstrate the validity of the approaches, achieving state infidelities smaller than $2\cdot 10^{-3}$ with success probabilities greater than $10^{-3}$, compatible with practical quantum state sampling. Overall, we observe that the QSVT method consistently delivers higher accuracy.
  We further observe that the condition number of the linear matrix, a key factor governing the performance of quantum solvers, saturates as the number of spatial lattice points increases. This implies that the spatial grid can be scaled to realistic industrial dimensions without increasing the HHL or QSVT circuit depth due to ill-conditioned matrices.

AI.tldr: This study evaluates quantum algorithms for computational electromagnetics, highlighting the advantages of QSVT over HHL in handling large-scale simulations efficiently with acceptable accuracy.
AI.motivation: To explore how quantum computing can enhance simulations in computational electromagnetics, particularly in addressing resource-intensive tasks through efficient algorithms.
AI.method: Performance analysis of the Harrow-Hassidim-Lloyd (HHL) and Quantum Singular Value Transformation (QSVT) algorithms for solving linear systems arising from the finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) method, benchmarked against industrial use cases.
AI.result: The QSVT method demonstrated higher accuracy compared to HHL, achieving an infidelity below $2\cdot 10^{-3}$ and successful probabilities exceeding $10^{-3}$.
AI.conclusion: Despite increasing spatial discretization, both algorithms maintain circuit depth, allowing scaling to industrial standards effectively, with performance influenced by the saturation of condition numbers.

title: Optimal fidelity estimation when one state is pure via algorithmic Uhlmann transform
summary:
The Uhlmann fidelity ${\rm F}(ρ_0,ρ_1) = {\rm tr}|\sqrt{ρ_0}\sqrt{ρ_1}|$ is one of the most fundamental quantities in quantum information theory for quantifying the closeness between two quantum states. Estimating the Uhlmann fidelity to within additive error $\varepsilon$ requires a number of copies of the states, or queries to their state-preparation circuits, that depends at least linearly on the smaller of the ranks of $ρ_0$ and $ρ_1$. Consequently, this rank dependence disappears when either state is pure, in which case the query and sample complexities depend only polynomially on $1/\varepsilon$. However, the known optimal estimator for ${\rm F}(ρ,|ψ\rangle\!\langleψ|)$ due to Fang and Wang (ESA 2025) requires prior knowledge of which state is pure.
  In this work, we remove this mathematically unnecessary prior-knowledge requirement and establish an optimal estimator for ${\rm F}(ρ, |ψ\rangle\!\langleψ|)$ under the sole promise that one of the two states is pure, without knowing which one. Our estimator is obtained by specializing the refined algorithmic Uhlmann transform of Utsumi, Nakata, Wang, and Takagi (2025) to the case where one state is pure. In this setting, the Uhlmann fidelity can be recovered as follows: apply a unitary dilation of ${\rm tr}_{\sf A}(|ψ_0\rangle\!\langleψ_1|)$ (or its inverse) to the reference register $\sf R$ of the purification $|ψ_1\rangle$ (or $|ψ_0\rangle$) on the registers $\sf A$ and $\sf R$, estimate the corresponding square-root amplitude in each case, and take the maximum of the resulting two estimates.

AI.tldr: This paper presents an optimal estimator for Uhlmann fidelity between quantum states with one pure state, removing the prior knowledge requirement.
AI.motivation: To improve the estimation of Uhlmann fidelity without needing to know which quantum state is pure.
AI.method: The method uses a refined algorithmic Uhlmann transform, applying unitary dilations and estimating square-root amplitudes.
AI.result: The estimator achieves optimal performance by maximizing two estimates derived from the quantum states.
AI.conclusion: The study enhances the efficiency of fidelity estimation in quantum information theory under relaxed conditions.

title: Helium-like ions $(Z,e,e)$ in Lagrange Mesh method, interpolating the highly-accurate energy spectra vs. Z
summary: Two alternative approaches for studying Helium-like atomic ions in non-relativistic quantum mechanics are proposed: (I) a numerical approach, based on the Lagrange-mesh method which can easily reach up to 14-15 significant digits in the energy spectrum for any nuclear charge $Z$ with modest CPU time in single processor mode and (II) a highly-accurate, few-parametric interpolation formula for the energies {\it vs.} $Z$. The interpolation formula of general nature is proposed, it can be applied to the energies of any excited state of the helium-like sequence. It is based on matching the $1/Z$-expansion at large $Z$ and the Puiseux expansion with integer and half-integer powers around the so-called second critical charge $Z_B$, introduced by F and D Stillinger (1969, 1974), confirmed by the present authors in 2019 for the ground state $1^1 S$, then revisited here, and extended to the excited states in the present work. For example for the first two spin-singlet $1^1 S$, $2^1 S$ and the first two spin-triplet $2^3 S$, $3^3 S$ states this interpolation formula with nine free parameters can reach an accuracy of 10-14 significant digits (s.d.) in the energies for any physically-relevant nuclear charge $Z$, giving absolute accuracy at large $Z$. Many results are obtained for the first time.

AI.tldr: The paper presents two methods for studying Helium-like ions in non-relativistic quantum mechanics: a numerical Lagrange-mesh method for precise energy calculations and an interpolation formula for estimating energy states based on varying nuclear charges.
AI.motivation: Understanding energy states of Helium-like atomic ions is crucial for various applications in atomic physics and quantum mechanics. Achieving high accuracy in energy calculations is a significant challenge.
AI.method: The research introduces a Lagrange-mesh numerical approach for energy spectrum calculations, achieving high precision, and develops a few-parametric interpolation formula based on $1/Z$ and Puiseux expansions to estimate energies for varying nuclear charges.
AI.result: The interpolation formula shows an accuracy of up to 10-14 significant digits for several excited states across a range of nuclear charges, achieving absolute accuracy at large $Z$ and providing new results not previously documented.
